decisions.rationale: Names one specific disease, familial deficiency of the seventh complement component (C7 deficiency), with a single definition and no further subdivision.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 - Specific Disease; Examples 6

decisions.rationale: Refers to a family of bacteremic infections (recurrent episodes of several possible infections) rather than one specific disease definition.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 - Disease Class; Examples 10 and 11

decisions.rationale: Neisseria is only an organism name here, given as the cause of the infections; organism names are not annotated unless the disease they cause is clearly the subject, and the disease is already covered by other spans.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 - Organism names

decisions.rationale: Disseminated gonococcal infection is a specific clinical disease entity with one definition (gonorrhea spread beyond the local site), not a general category.
Contiguous string containing two separate disease mentions (meningococcal meningitis and arthritis) that cannot be split without information loss.

decisions.rationale: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is named only as the organism targeted by complement-mediated bactericidal activity in the lab context; the disease it causes is not being discussed.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 1 - Organism names; Examples 4

decisions.rationale: The word syndrome is a very general term that does not name a specific disease on its own.
